name.en: Make a dashboard from my data
name.es: Crear un panel (dashboard) con mis datos

description.en: Builds one offline HTML dashboard with KPI cards, charts and filters from your data file.
description.es: Arma un dashboard HTML que funciona sin internet, con tarjetas de indicadores, gráficos y filtros a partir de tus datos.

label.es: Tu archivo de datos (CSV o Excel)

nodes.text:
Build a dashboard from the data file {{inputFile}} (inside data/). What it should show: {{what}}

Requirements:
- ONE self-contained HTML file: outputs/dashboard.html. Embed the data (aggregated if large) as JSON inside the file, and draw the charts with inline JavaScript using SVG or canvas. No external network: no CDN, no web fonts. It must work offline by double-clicking.
- A row of KPI cards for the key numbers, 3 to 5 charts that fit the data (bars, lines, pie/donut only if few categories), a sortable table of the details, and filters (for example by date range and category) that update every chart and KPI.
- Clean, accessible design: readable colours with good contrast, labelled axes, tooltips on hover, responsive layout, sensible number and date formats.
- Read the data with Python (pandas), clean it on a copy (never change the original), and generate the HTML from a small script saved in outputs/build_dashboard.py so it can be regenerated.
- Optional extra only: at the end, mention in one sentence that a Streamlit version is possible if the user later wants a live app. Do not build it unless asked.

GROUND RULES (follow strictly):
- Any user-provided input file lives in data/ inside this project. NEVER modify, move or delete the originals: work on copies inside the project.
- Put every deliverable in outputs/ (create the folder if needed). Do not write deliverables anywhere else.
- Prefer Python. Use the Python packages already installed globally; create a virtual environment (python -m venv .venv) ONLY if a needed package is missing, and pip install ONLY what you need from: openpyxl pandas xlsxwriter matplotlib python-docx. If Python is not installed or cannot be run, say so plainly in one short message and STOP (do not try to install Python yourself).
- Do not ask questions mid-way unless you are truly blocked. Instead, make sensible choices and write your assumptions down in the deliverable and in your final message.
- Write the deliverables and the final message in the same language as the user's request (Spanish or English).
- Be safe: do not run anything destructive, do not touch files outside this project, do not send data over the network (except where this task explicitly needs web search).
- FINISH with a short plain-language summary for a non-technical person: what you produced, where it is (exact paths under outputs/), the assumptions you made, and anything they should double-check.

nodes.message: Open outputs/dashboard.html in your browser, try the filters and check the numbers. Approve if it is right.
